page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 96 vCPUs and 360 GB of memory across 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with simultaneous multithreading enabled, the instance provides 504 MB of shared L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions for advanced matrix operations, machine learning acceleration, and cryptography.

Integrated directly into the instance is 6432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 16 drives, while no discrete GPUs are bundled. Benchmark measurements demonstrate top-tier execution in compute-heavy and I/O-intensive workloads, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 110513.48, high compilation throughput in Clang (69152.0), and 171.76 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Memory throughput remains robust, recording 356.38 GB/sec in large-block read testing.

Given its density of compute resources, multi-terabyte local NVMe subsystem, and high memory bandwidth, the c4-standard-96-lssd offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource consolidation. It is well-matched for large relational databases, in-memory caches, distributed build and CI/CD pipelines, high-throughput static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96-lssd is a high-capacity general-purpose virtual machine configured with 96 vCPUs and 360 GB of system memory, driven by a 48-core Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it incorporates a 504 MB L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector extensions including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance bundles 6432 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across 16 disks, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results indicate exceptional throughput across parallel tasks, including top-tier Redis SET operations at 171.76 million ops/sec, strong Clang software compilation, and PassMark database processing scores exceeding 34,100. The balanced ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU combined with extensive local NVMe capacity delivers high architectural efficiency for IOPS-demanding transactional databases, real-time analytics, large caching layers, continuous integration pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
